column1: # Cards written by hand, for a reading no engine proposed — the follow-up a
# Five TAB-separated fields. Blank lines and `#` lines are ignored, and
# `becomes` may be empty (a deletion). `token` must be unique on its line,
# and `source` becomes the button's name, so it must say who read the ink.
# ⚠ CHANGING `site` OR `token` AFTER A RULING RENAMES THE CARD and orphans
# the answer. Fix the `why`, never the key.

you ruled this line whole on 2026-08-13 and the acute went to the α; ruling its parts on 08-14 you put it over the υ. At 9× the mark is a straight tick over the υ and the α is bare — not the curl a breathing makes in this font (compare ἀνδρῶν on this line)

the line is otherwise fully accented and both engines read it bare; at 9× there is a faint tick over the α, far lighter than the acute on μόνον beside it. Doubtful ink — if the print really is bare, keep it and mark the erratum
nothing over the first α, and a short stroke over the last that leans the way the grave on ϗ̀ beside it leans. Bare of breathing as printed, so the diplomatic reading is αλλὰ and not ἀλλὰ

John, 2026-08-15, reading the crop: "should be (τὸν ὦτον)". `[?]` is a transcription placeholder, not ink; calamari read ὦτον out-of-fold and kraken read υὦτον
John, 2026-08-15: "there is nothing before the ὁ". Both engines read nothing there, and the quotation has no closing mark either, so no opening quote is missing
John, 2026-08-15: "it's 'ad l l cf C).'" — two Latin ells with a space, not eleven. calamari read `ad l 1 cf` out-of-fold and had the space but only one of the ells; no card could offer both
John, 2026-08-15: "it's 'αἷμα ὡς φασὶν'". The engines read υὧς — they kept the υ nobody prints — and the sense wants it: "the dark one, as they say, sheds blood from the eyes"

the mark is the IOTA SUBSCRIPT of τῇ on the line above, hanging into this one — it aligns under the ῇ of ἀκολȣθεῖ τῇ and belongs to that line, not this. calamari read (Hom λ 598) out-of-fold with nothing there; kraken picked the descender up as an apostrophe
